title: kv: improved KV cache memory management and eviction (fragmentation, paging, spillover)
author: Maya Chen
description: Motivation: the existing KV cache shows pathological fragmentation and high OOM/miss rates under heterogeneous sequence-length workloads and high-concurrency continuous-batching. Small allocation churn and variable KV sizes cause memory holes that are not reclaimable by the allocator, and when host memory is available we lacked a safe, async spillover mechanism. This PR introduces a multi-layer solution: 1) slab-aware KV allocator and periodic compaction to reduce fragmentation and make eviction decisions cheaper; 2) size-bucketed LRU eviction with heuristics that prefer spilling low-reuse or large cold entries; 3) paged spillover to host RAM with async writeback/readback and a residency table to track resident pages vs spilled pages; 4) prefetch/pin hooks exposed to the continuous-batching scheduler so hot contexts can be prefetched and pinned to avoid page faults during low-latency responses; 5) scheduler policy change to prefer requests with resident KV working sets and to apply backpressure when spill/writeback is saturated; 6) extensive telemetry and tracing (fragmentation ratio, page-faults, bytes-spilled, spill-latency, compaction time) and safety checks for concurrent compaction/eviction. The description below contains a checklist and short usage notes. Checklist: - [x] slab allocator implementation and unit tests; - [x] eviction policy and residency table; - [x] async spill/writeback and readback path; - [x] scheduler integration and prefetch hooks; - [x] telemetry, counters and dashboards; - [x] benchmarks and microbench tests showing regression/no-regression; - [x] docs and configuration knobs (spill_threshold, page_size, async_window, compaction_interval). Backwards compatibility: default behavior is unchanged unless the operator enables spillover or reduces spill_threshold; all knobs are runtime-configurable. Impact: in our internal perf lab, this reduces OOM events by ~30% on mixed-length workloads and reduces 95th latency by ~10–15% in high-concurrency scenarios due to fewer page-fault stalls. See 'files_changed' for integration points and 'review_comments' for discussion details.
commit_summary: 5 commits: implement slab allocator + compaction; add paged spillover (async IO) and residency table; new size-bucketed LRU eviction policy; scheduler prefetch & pin hooks; telemetry, tests, and docs
review_comments: Arjun Patel (review): Overall approach LGTM, good separation between allocator and eviction. Please add more unit tests for concurrent compaction + eviction races; the current test covers single-threaded compaction only.
Maya Chen (author): Added concurrent compaction tests and a small stress harness that runs compaction + evictions under synthetic workloads; tests added in tests/kv/kv_eviction_test.cpp.

Lena Gomez (review): Concern: async spillback/readback can introduce jitter under load. Can we expose an operator-visible backpressure metric and ensure scheduler yields instead of overloading async io? Also please document the failure modes for readback latency.

Maya Chen (author): Exposed spill_io_utilization and spill_queue_length metrics; scheduler now checks spill_io_utilization>0.85 before prefetching and will fall back to eviction without prefetch. Added docs in docs/perf/kv-eviction-paging-spillover.md.

Diego Martinez (review): Nit: please ensure kernel-level pin/unpin API is no-op when page-based spill is disabled (to avoid regressions for dedicated deployments). Also add a short compatibility test for Dedicated vs Hosted modes.
Maya Chen (author): Updated APIs: kernel_pin/kernal_unpin are guarded by runtime config; added a smoke test that runs in both Hosted and Dedicated CI profiles.
Arjun Patel (approval): Verified unit tests and benchmarks. Bench numbers: 30% fewer OOMs on perf-lab mixed sequences, 12% end-to-end latency improvement on high-concurrency trace. Approving.
CI: Build passed on Linux/gcc and macOS/clang; flaky test kv_paging_integration_test retried once and passed. All checks green.
release_notes: Improved KV cache memory management: slab allocator and compaction to reduce fragmentation; size-bucketed LRU eviction; paged spillover to host RAM with async writeback/readback; scheduler prefetch/pin integration to reduce page-fault stalls; new telemetry for fragmentation and spill metrics; runtime knobs for tuning spill thresholds and compaction interval; default behavior unchanged unless spillover enabled.
notes_for_ops: Config knobs: spill_threshold (bytes), page_size (KB), async_window_ms, compaction_interval_ms. Default: spill_threshold=0 (disabled) to preserve previous behavior. Enable spillover to allow host-memory fallback. Monitor telemetry: kv_fragmentation_ratio, kv_spilled_bytes, spill_io_utilization, spill_queue_length.
benchmarks_summary: Internal perf-lab: mixed-length 1000-concurrent sessions: OOM rate down 30%, 95th latency down 10–15% when spillover enabled with prefetching; microbench of compaction shows average compaction pause 2.4ms at 99th. Bench scripts included under scripts/benchmarks.
squash_notes: Squashed feature work: primary author Maya Chen; includes allocator, paging, scheduler hooks, telemetry and tests. See commit messages for incremental rationale.
